title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of a health claim related to oat beta-glucan and lowering blood cholesterol and reduced risk of (coronary) heart disease pursuant to Article 14 of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the Competent Authority of the United Kingdom following an application by CreaNutrition AG (Question EFSA-Q-2008-681). The evidence assessed was supplied by the applicant, which claimed proprietary rights and confidentiality for three unpublished studies and one unpublished meta-analysis.
result: Oat beta-glucan is a non-digestible linear glucose polymer with mixed beta-(1-4) and beta-(1-3) links in an approximate ratio of 70% to 30%, occurring naturally in oat bran. In the unpublished meta-analysis submitted by the applicant as proprietary (Whitehead 2008, MPS Research Unit, Lancaster University) of 18 studies (1080 subjects, 3 to 9 g/d, 2 to 12 weeks), total cholesterol changed by -0.34 mmol/L (95% CI -0.42 to -0.25) and LDL cholesterol by -0.28 mmol/L (-0.35 to -0.22); the fitted effect of 3 g/d was -0.21 mmol/L (-0.31 to -0.11) for LDL cholesterol. Proposed mechanism: increased small-intestinal viscosity reduces bile acid reabsorption. The Panel concluded that a cause and effect relationship is established between oat beta-glucan and lowering of blood LDL cholesterol, and that foods bearing the claim should provide at least 3 g oat beta-glucan per day. The Panel could have reached this conclusion without considering the studies claimed by the applicant as proprietary.
